author: UzmiGames
clean_room: Written from the public papers, books and standards below only. No Adobe code, asset, output or documentation of Substance internals was used; no primitive is fitted to Painter.

sources.title: IEEE 754-2019, Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic
sources.facts: Correct rounding of the square root to nearest, ties to even.

sources.title: H. S. Warren, Hacker's Delight, 2nd ed., 2012
sources.facts: The bit-by-bit integer square root and its remainder.

primitives.notes: Computed on integers so that GPU and CPU agree; equals the host's IEEE sqrt on 1.04 M tested values.

sources.title: M. Jarzynski, M. Olano, Hash Functions for GPU Rendering, JCGT 9(3), 2020
sources.facts: The LCG step, the two cross-multiplication rounds and the 16-bit xorshift.

primitives.notes: Used in place of Perlin's permutation table for lattice hashing; the seed enters as a per-seed offset of the lattice key (a UzmiGames choice).

sources.title: K. Perlin, An Image Synthesizer, SIGGRAPH 1985
sources.facts: Pseudo-random gradients on the integer lattice, dot products with the corner offsets, interpolation by 3t^2 - 2t^3.

primitives.notes: Gradient components are uniform in [-1, 1) from the hash (not normalised: a normalisation needs a square root and a division).

sources.title: K. Perlin, Improving Noise, SIGGRAPH 2002 (ACM TOG 21(3))
sources.section: The interpolant and the gradient set
sources.facts: The interpolant 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3 and the twelve cube-edge gradients selected by four hash bits.

primitives.notes: The paper's permutation table is replaced by Pcg3d.

sources.title: K. Perlin, Noise Hardware, Real-Time Shading SIGGRAPH Course Notes, 2001
sources.facts: Noise over the simplicial lattice with radially symmetric corner kernels.

sources.title: S. Gustavson, Simplex Noise Demystified, 2005
sources.facts: Skew and unskew factors 1/3 and 1/6, ranking of the offsets, kernel (0.6 - d^2)^4, gradients from the twelve cube edges, scale 32.

sources.title: S. Worley, A Cellular Texture Basis Function, SIGGRAPH 1996
sources.facts: Feature points scattered per cell, F1 and F2 as the nearest and second-nearest distances, alternative distance metrics.

primitives.notes: One feature point per cell and the 27 neighbouring cells, as is usual in GPU implementations; Euclidean, Manhattan and Chebyshev metrics.

sources.title: B. B. Mandelbrot, J. W. Van Ness, Fractional Brownian Motions, Fractional Noises and Applications, SIAM Review 10(4), 1968
D. S. Ebert, F. K. Musgrave et al., Texturing and Modeling: A Procedural Approach, 3rd ed., 2003
sources.section: F. K. Musgrave's chapters on fractal models (fBm)
sources.facts: The spectral sum of octaves with lacunarity and gain.

primitives.notes: Octave i uses seed + i; the sum is not normalised.

sources.title: J. Serra, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology, 1982
sources.facts: Grey-scale dilation by a flat structuring element (maximum over the element).

sources.title: R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, 4th ed., 2018
sources.facts: Flat square and disk structuring elements.

primitives.notes: Wrap or clamp borders; strict comparison so NaN never wins.

sources.title: J. Serra, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology, 1982
sources.facts: Grey-scale erosion by a flat structuring element (minimum), the dual of dilation.

primitives.notes: Tested as the exact dual of Dilate.

sources.title: R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, 4th ed., 2018
sources.facts: Separable linear filters applied as a horizontal then a vertical pass.

primitives.notes: Taps summed in a fixed order from offset -r to r.

sources.title: R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, 4th ed., 2018
R. C. Gonzalez, R. E. Woods, Digital Image Processing, 4th ed., 2018
sources.facts: Weights exp(-k^2 / (2 sigma^2)), normalised to sum 1.

primitives.notes: The exponential is evaluated with IEEE double additions, multiplications and divisions only (halving, a Taylor series, squaring), so every machine computes the same weights.
